summary: Former Dickenson County tower; a Dickenson Star headline reports that only a concrete pier remains.

facts.status_note: Tower gone; a newspaper headline reports that a concrete pier is all that remains.

evidence.supports: Listed as a tower, now gone, in Dickenson County at 37.13570, -82.33777
Post office at Nealy Ridge opened in 1909 and closed in 1961
evidence.quote: A post office was established at Nealy Ridge in 1909, and remained in operation until it was discontinued in 1961.

evidence.supports: Headline (article body paywalled, not read) says only a concrete pier is left of the tower
evidence.quote: Concrete pier all that remains of Nealy Ridge fire tower

evidence.supports: Byline credits the author as Dickenson County Historical Society vice-president

sources.title: Concrete pier all that remains of Nealy Ridge fire tower

notes_for_editor: The Dickenson Star article is paywalled. Only its headline and byline could be read, and its date is unknown, so the pier claim rests on the headline alone. Two searches found no build, staffing or removal dates. The post office facts come from Wikipedia and describe the place, not the tower. The article may describe the society's search for records of the towers, but that appears only in a search snippet and is not used.
